items.title: Tired of paying for cloud storage every month? pCloud’s Black Friday Lifetime deal is the cure for subscription fatigue
items.summary:
Software used to be a one-time purchase, but over time, with the addition of cloud storage and services, everything has become a subscription. One company even tried to make your car seat heaters a subscription . Count the subscriptions you’re paying for right now: iCloud, a password manager, a couple of streaming services, a music service, maybe a VPN, and whatever other app decided this year that it needed to be $4.99 per month for something that used to be a one-time purchase.

Everything is a service now, and a lot of people are hitting the point where one more monthly charge is one too many on principle alone. items.title: Google Pixel bug reveals hidden Private Space when switching between light and dark mode
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google’s November 2026 Pixel update still hasn’t fixed a Private Space bug that first surfaced in September. 
 Switching between light and dark modes causes the hidden Private Space section to reappear in the app drawer, even when it’s set to remain hidden. 
 Google has acknowledged a potentially related issue on its Issue Tracker, but there’s no confirmed fix yet. 

Google’s big November update packs dozens of bug fixes , but a recent Private Space issue, which unhides the hidden folder in the app drawer, appears to have again slipped through the cracks. For reference, the bug first surfaced following Android 17 QPR1 in September. Fast-forward to Android 17 QPR2 , and the bug is still there.

For those unaware, Pixel’s Private Space lets you create a sandbox within your phone. It essentially acts as a separate, locked space where you can keep apps, folders, files, and anything that you want to keep away from prying eyes. The locked space appears at the bottom of the Pixel app drawer, though users also have the option to completely hide the space’s existence.
items.t: Google Pixel bug reveals hidden Private Space when switching between light and dark mode

items.title: Google gets ready to kill off Pixel 10 Magic Cue in favor of Proactive Assistance
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Magic Cue launched on Pixel 10 phones, offering to find useful info in your apps and bring it to your attention. 
 Proactive Assistance debuted with the Pixel 11 series, working quite similarly to Magic Cue, and we’ve been wondering if it’s meant to replace it. 
 New text strings now highlight Google’s plans to move Magic Cue users to Proactive Assistance by the end of 2027. 

Google first introduced Proactive Assistance with the Pixel 11 series this year, and now it looks like the company is getting ready to fully replace Magic Cue with its new system — eventually.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Magic Cue debuted with Pixel 10 phones, attempting to proactively surface information from apps around your phone when you need it most. But then when we got Proactive Assistance on the Pixel 11 , it largely just felt like more of the same. We even looked at some evidence that seemed to support the idea that Proactive Assistance might be designed as a replacement for Magic Cue .
items.t: Google gets ready to kill off Pixel 10 Magic Cue in favor of Proactive Assistance

items.title: OpenAI rolls out ChatGPT Wallet to let Dots AI agents make purchases
items.summary:
TL;DR 

OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet to let its Dots AI agents make purchases for users. 
 Wallet is available to US-based ChatGPT Pro subscribers who have a US-issued Visa, Mastercard, or American Express. 
 The move comes as some retailers and service providers ban AI agents from their platforms. 

OpenAI’s Dots personal AI agents are gaining the ability to shop, with the launch of ChatGPT Wallet today. The digital wallet substitutes a payment token for a user’s credit card details and lets its Dot make purchases.

ChatGPT Wallet is available to US-based ChatGPT Pro subscribers who have a US-issued Visa, Mastercard, or American Express card. OpenAI said that while Dots will assist in the purchase process, users will review the items, be apprised of the total, select the card to use, and approve the purchase with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. The goal, though, is for the agents to ultimately have more control.
items.t: OpenAI rolls out ChatGPT Wallet to let Dots AI agents make purchases

items.title: Recompa simplifies Android handheld installs so you can spend more time playing
items.summary:
Credit: Nathan Lohnes 

TL;DR 

Recompa is an app that finds and installs decompilations and native ports that work with Android devices and handhelds. 
 The app provides a more seamless way to search for and install games and apps than looking through GitHub. 
 While it’s designed for handhelds, it also works with phones and tablets. 

Now that all colors of the Retroid Pocket Duo are shipping , it’s time to start thinking about the games you’ll put on it. While GitHub has thousands of decompilations to choose from, finding and downloading the files you want can be a burdensome task. If you’re not all that familiar with using GitHub, there’s something you can use to make searching for and installing games on your Android handheld much easier.

That’s where the Android app known as Recompa comes into play. This app is designed to simplify the sourcing and installation of decompilations and native ports. Recompa organizes these decompilations and ports as if they were in a marketplace, making the act of searching for and exploring games far easier. When you find the title you’re looking for, you can install it with the press of a button.
items.t: Recompa simplifies Android handheld installs so you can spend more time playing

items.title: Google’s November Pixel update is leaving screensavers stuck at full brightness
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Pixel users are reporting that their screensavers’ low-light mode has stopped working properly after Google’s November update. 
 Affected users say their screensavers remain unusually bright at night, with some reporting that manually lowering the brightness only helps temporarily. 
 The issue doesn’t appear to be widespread, and there’s no confirmed fix yet. 

Google’s big November update seems to have broken a lot of features , and Pixel’s low-light mode for screensavers is the latest casualty. Several Pixel users have taken to platforms like Reddit and the Google Support forum to report that their phones’ screensavers aren’t dimming while charging at night. Naturally, this is leaving users with unusually bright bedrooms.

For reference, the feature, which can be accessed via Settings > Display & touch > Screen saver, lets you select a built-in screensaver that appears while your device is charging. It can be set to only show while charging, while upright and charging, or only while wirelessly charging. Considering that a lot of us charge our phones overnight, the accompanying low-light mode is a nifty addition that ensures screensavers adjust to the surrounding lighting conditions.
items.t: Google’s November Pixel update is leaving screensavers stuck at full brightness

 Google support has contacted affected users and escalated recent complaints to the Android Auto team, but there’s no confirmed fix. 

Steering-wheel buttons are supposed to make controlling music easier while driving, but some Android Auto users are finding that a single press can send their playlists two songs forward or backward. It’s a frustrating problem that has been around for months, and fresh complaints suggest it isn’t going away anytime soon.

The issue first gained attention earlier this year , when owners of the 2026 Toyota RAV4 reported that pressing the next or previous button on their steering wheels registered two commands instead of one. The behavior affected multiple music apps, including Spotify and YouTube Music, across wired and wireless connections.

items.summary:
Samsung was the undisputed foldable king in the third quarter of this year, reports Smart Analytics Global (SAG) based on data from its Smartphone 360 research service. Overall, the foldable market shrank 2% year-over-year to 7.5 million units shipped for the three-month period.

Samsung held 69% market share, its highest since 2023. Meanwhile, Huawei lost 4 percentage points, but remains in second place. Lenovo/Motorola gained 2 percentage points as it rolled out the Razr 70 series to new regions. As for other brands, their market share declined significantly.
